compsNote: 3 of the 3 competitors are within 1 km. Only executive condos are compared (an EC sells below private condos because of its buyer rules). Near-twins come first: up to two condos within 1.5 km with a similar number of homes (half to double) completed in 2016 or later. Then every suitable condo within 1 km (same tenure, completed 2011 or later first), widening to 2 km and 3 km only if fewer than 3. Resale ECs past their 5-year minimum occupation period sell to any Singaporean or PR. Resale prices are URA medians for the last 6 months where there were at least 5 resales, otherwise the last 12 months. Condos launched before June 2023 measured their areas under the old rules (including air-con ledges), so their psf is raised 5% to compare like for like.
priceDecide: Like for like by size: for each unit type we take each resale competitor's average psf for units within about 15% of that size (last 6 months, or 12 or 24 if too few). Each is raised by the 32% new-launch premium that launches selling now in the OCR carry over their closest resale (12 launches). Buy at or below = the average of the competitors' new-launch equivalents for that size; walk away above = 5% more. 3-bed: buy at or below $1,700, walk away above $1,780, this project about $1,796 psf; 4-bed: buy at or below $1,700, walk away above $1,780, this project about $1,805 psf. This project's price by unit type is from the developer's caveats.  The developer breaks even at about $1,450 psf (EdgeProp's method); launches since 2023 priced on average 27% above break-even, which points to about $1,840 psf.

gain.timeline: Buy now (November 2026) at the current average. Completion: Keys by 31 Mar 2029. The 5-year minimum occupation period then runs to about 2034, when any Singaporean or PR can buy it. We look at a sale in 2034 (8 years).
gain.costs: No Seller's Stamp Duty: the sale is after the 5-year minimum occupation period. Potential gain is after Buyer's Stamp Duty at IRAS rates, about $6,000 legal fees and a 2% agent fee plus 9% GST when you sell. Loan interest, property tax, maintenance and rent are not included.

exit.note: At launch an EC bought from the developer is capped by the 30% mortgage servicing ratio (MSR) and a $16,000 household income ceiling; resale buyers after the minimum occupation period face only the 55% TDSR. How we test each buyer group, in today's money (prices, HDB values and incomes tend to rise together): the unit at today's current average price; a 25% down payment plus Buyer's Stamp Duty; HDB upgraders put their flat's sale proceeds in first (median resale price, minus an illustrative $150,000 loan). The group can buy if that capital covers the down payment and stamp duty; the income the remaining 30-year loan needs (tested at 4% under the 55% TDSR) is shown against SingStat's 2025 averages by home type, excluding employer CPF (4-room $11,097, 5-room and executive $13,887, condo $22,006). HDB resale prices rose 4.2% a year over the past 10 years, so upgraders' capital usually grows too. Singaporean HDB owners who buy before selling pay 20% Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty upfront and get it back only if they sell the flat within 6 months (IRAS).
exit.line: In this mixed own-stay and rental area, the 3-bed resale pool is wide; the 4-bed resale pool is good.

Score out of 10, same rules for every plan: start at 4; +1 regular shape, dumbbell, kitchen that can be closed off, kitchen or yard window, AC ledge and planter under 5%, store or shelter or utility room; −1 long corridor, ledge and planter 10% or more, balcony over 12%.
